subject: Renewal: Retainer-style advance credit proposal for 2027
messages:

Date: 2027-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning — looking to lock rates

Hi Laura,

We're starting renewal planning for our AI stack and are concerned about potential rate increases next year. The leadership team asked whether we can get a multi-year rate anchor — ideally by prepaying or setting up an advance-credit retainer that would hold 2027 rates for 24 months. Can Redwood do a structure like that, and how would ramping work if our usage grows?

Also cc'ing procurement.

Thanks,
Adeola
Director of AI Platforms
Acme Corp
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Adeola Johnson <adeola@acme.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-11T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — looking to lock rates

Hi Adeola — great to hear from you and glad you're starting early.

Short answer: yes — we offer a retainer-style advance credit arrangement that accomplishes a rate anchor across years while allowing a staged ramp. I've attached a short proposal that outlines two options:
- Multi-year retainer (24 months) with an upfront credit purchase at a 10% discount to public rates and an agreed ramp schedule;
- Hybrid prepay + overage model (lower upfront purchase, capped overage rates).

Key things to note: we can bake in a formal ramp schedule (monthly % increases that convert to committed units) and include a simple true-up each quarter. We can also add an automatic fallback to a nearby model variant if capacity is constrained.

I've attached the proposal (Redwood_Retainer_Proposal_v1.pdf) and a sample ramp workbook. Marcus is cc'd for commercial details and can re-run numbers against your usage profile.

Would you be available for a 30-minute call Wednesday to walk through the options?

Best,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Laura / Soojin — quick internal. I reviewed Acme's last 12 months; a 24-month retainer at ~9-12% discount looks viable if they prepay >= 60% of expected consumption year one. If they want a straight 24-month rate lock with lower upfront (40%), we should add quarterly true-ups and a built-in ramp credit (e.g., first 6 months at 0% growth, then staged).

Questions for the call:
- Do they need GAAP-friendly scheduling for the prepay? (procurement often asks)
- Any required audit/compliance holdbacks?
- Is the legal team going to request an SLA uplift?

I'll prepare two financial permutations for the call.

Marcus

Adeola — thanks for the redlines. Attached is an updated ramp workbook with quarter-by-quarter committed units and a sample true-up / invoice flow. Short answers:
- Ramp: we propose Q1 = baseline, Q2 = +15%, Q3 = +25%, Q4 = +40% (convertible to committed units in month 13). We can customize the percentages — the workbook is editable.
- Accounting: customers commonly treat upfront prepay as deferred expense; we'd provide an invoice with clear description, but Acme should confirm with your accounting team.
- Opt-out: we're comfortable with a 12-month material breach termination clause; legal will prepare language.

I've also included a DocuSign link for the 24-month retainer at the 10% discount if you want to move forward with the full upfront purchase. If you prefer the hybrid lane, we can generate that variant immediately after the call.
